thread:
Alice Morrow: Heads-up — customer ORD-442 reports console shows EU (ireland) for their org, but our request traces show a consistent serving region of us-east-2. They see +220ms p50. Ticket attached: https://support.redwood.ai/t/ORD-442
Raj Patel: Can you paste the trace IDs or a sample request?
Alice Morrow: Sure, sample trace header dump from their repro: `x-client-region: eu-west-1`, `x-org-id: org_443`, `request-id: rQ7b2f`
Alice Morrow: When we grep the serving logs for rQ7b2f we get: `served_region=us-east-2`, `backend_pool=dedicated-us`, `latency=238ms`
Leila Gomez: That sounds like our fallback behavior when local capacity is exhausted — we route to nearest available pool. Console label shows primary region, not where a request was actually served. Might be a visibility gap.
Charlie (SRE): Important: check the routing headers we emit. If console uses `preferred_region` but our route policy allowed `fallback_any_nearest`, it won't update console view. Need to confirm the routing decision TTL.
Raj Patel: Repro steps I ran from a eu VM: `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west-1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'`
Raj Patel: Response headers: `x-served-region: us-east-2`, `x-fallback-reason: capacity-unavailable`, `x-route-version: v12`
Alice Morrow: Customer also reported intermittent 401s when served from us-east-2 — they think their org token is region-scoped. Billing flagged because invoice view shows traffic in EU but actual serving was US so cost center mapping is off.
Leila Gomez: 401s could be caused by their token being restricted to eu-west-1 in our auth policy. If a token is region-scoped, cross-region serving should be rejected earlier. That mismatch is bad.
Charlie (SRE): Poking the routing table now. Found a recent change: `route-policy: prefer_primary_with_fallback_nearest` deployed 3h ago. It doesn't surface fallbacks to the console.
Charlie (SRE): Temporary mitigation: toggled `route-policy` back to `prefer_primary_with_local_queue` for org_443, forcing requests to queue rather than cross-region fallback. Will monitor latency.
Raj Patel: I pushed a hotfix to console code to show `last_actual_serving_region` in the per-request view (small PR, not yet released).
BillingBot: FYI — created invoice adjustment check ticket INV-119 for org_443 since served region differs from org region flag.
Alice Morrow: Customer notified of mitigation and offered two long-term options: 1) pin to dedicated capacity in EU, 2) enable explicit cross-region allowance for their tokens.
Leila Gomez: Action items: (1) SRE to annotate routing decisions in traces (Charlie), (2) Auth to support region-agnostic tokens or clearer 401 message (Raj), (3) Console to surface serving region per-request (Raj), (4) Billing follow-up (Billing).
Charlie (SRE): Monitoring: after toggle, p50 dropped to 35ms for their EU repro. Leaving toggle for 2 hours before grad rollback.
Alice Morrow: Marking this thread resolved for support until we confirm rollback. Customer content with mitigation. Will follow up on INV-119 and the console PR. :white_check_mark:
